categories.label: Persistent guidance
categories.evaluate: `AGENTS.md` or equivalent exists and is concise, accurate, and limited to non-inferable guidance: exact commands, safety boundaries, and pointers to canonical docs. Reward brevity; long always-on files and content an agent could infer from the code are quality risks. Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` natively unless a `CLAUDE.md` shadows it without importing it; root `.cursorrules` counts as deprecated persistent guidance; nested guidance is expected only for multi-project or multi-service repos

categories.label: Scoped rules
categories.evaluate: Cursor/Copilot/Claude path-scoped rules exist where useful, are actionable, and keep guidance out of always-on context

categories.label: Skills
categories.evaluate: `SKILL.md` packages cover repeated workflows with clear triggers, a `name` matching the skill directory, and supporting files where useful; portable `.agents/skills` locations work across the most agents. Legacy prompt files and commands earn partial credit
guidanceSections: 3.5 Commands, prompt files, and reusable workflows

categories.label: Specialized agents
categories.evaluate: Verifier, test, security, debug, or other focused agents exist where useful and use least-privilege tools. Evidence for performance benefit is limited, so do not treat missing agents as a major gap for simple repos

categories.label: Tool manifests and MCP
categories.evaluate: External tools are configured only where needed, secrets are externalized, and access is governed. Score as neutral (full or near-full credit) when the repo shows no external-system need; reduce the score only when an external need exists without governed access, or when MCP/tool configs are ungoverned, unpinned, or hold secrets

categories.label: Validation and reproducibility
categories.evaluate: Agent-readable validation commands, including a narrow single-file or single-package test command, match real scripts/CI; the environment is reproducible through lockfiles, devcontainers, or cloud-agent setup such as `copilot-setup-steps.yml` or setup scripts

categories.label: CI and PR automation
categories.evaluate: CI validates normal work and checks agent assets or AI-assisted PRs where appropriate

categories.label: Security, sandboxing, and hooks
categories.evaluate: Hooks, deny rules, sandbox settings, approvals, and secret controls exist for risky workflows

categories.label: Domain and decision context
categories.evaluate: ADRs, contracts, glossary, examples, fixtures, and templates are available and referenced
guidanceSections: 3.10 Domain context: ADRs, contracts, examples, and fixtures

categories.label: Governance and observability
categories.evaluate: Owners, review cadence, managed settings, logs, metrics, or dashboards exist where appropriate

categories.label: Versioning and dependency provenance
categories.evaluate: Agent assets are version-controlled; executable MCP/hook/skill dependencies are pinned or governed

categories.label: Onboarding and discoverability
categories.evaluate: README or equivalent tells humans where agent guidance, rules, skills, and workflows live

bands.label: Fragile
bands.interpretation: Agent behavior is mostly implicit, ad hoc, or person-dependent

bands.label: Emerging
bands.interpretation: Some useful artifacts exist, but they are incomplete or not yet reliable controls

bands.label: Operational
bands.interpretation: Agents can work productively with moderate safety and repeatability

bands.label: Managed
bands.interpretation: Context, tools, validation, and governance are integrated into normal engineering workflow

bands.label: Mature
bands.interpretation: Repo supports scalable, governed, observable, multi-agent operation
